req.title: Reuse db connection per request
req.statement: The system shall reuse a single sqlite3 connection per Flask request via flask.g.

doc.reasoning: R-FLASKR-025 requires that a single sqlite3 connection is reused per Flask request via flask.g. The key invariant is: within one request context, get_db() called multiple times must return the exact same connection object (identity check, not just equality). Across separate requests, connections may differ. We test: (1) positive — two calls to get_db() within one app context return the same object; (2) negative — after teardown (close_db), g no longer holds 'db', so a fresh call creates a new connection; (3) boundary — calling get_db() exactly once vs. twice within the same context, verifying the 'db' key is set in g after the first call and that the second call does not create a new connection. We also verify the connection has row_factory set to sqlite3.Row, catching mutations to that assignment.

tests.name: test_get_db_reuses_same_connection_within_request
preconditions: Flask app created with TESTING=True and a temp DATABASE path
Database initialised via init_db()
An active app context is pushed
actions: Push an application context
Call flaskr.db.get_db() a first time, store result as conn1
Call flaskr.db.get_db() a second time, store result as conn2
Assert conn1 is conn2 (identity, not equality)
expected: Both calls return the identical sqlite3.Connection object
flask.g contains key 'db' after first call
trace: R-FLASKR-025: connection reuse per request via flask.g
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db, init_db
from flask import g

def test_get_db_reuses_same_connection_within_request():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite')
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        init_db()
        conn1 = get_db()
        conn2 = get_db()
        assert conn1 is conn2, "get_db() must return the same connection object within one request"
        assert 'db' in g.__dict__ or hasattr(g, 'db'), "flask.g must hold 'db' after get_db()"

test_get_db_reuses_same_connection_within_request()

tests.name: test_get_db_creates_new_connection_after_close_db
preconditions: Flask app created with TESTING=True and a temp DATABASE path
Database initialised via init_db()
An active app context is pushed
actions: Push an application context
Call get_db() to obtain conn1
Call close_db() to tear down the connection and remove 'db' from g
Call get_db() again to obtain conn2
Assert conn1 is NOT conn2
expected: After close_db(), 'db' is removed from g
A subsequent get_db() call creates a brand-new connection object distinct from the first
trace: R-FLASKR-025: close_db removes connection from g; next get_db() must create fresh one
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db, init_db, close_db
from flask import g

def test_get_db_creates_new_connection_after_close_db():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite')
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        init_db()
        conn1 = get_db()
        close_db()
        # After close_db, 'db' must not be in g
        assert not hasattr(g, 'db') or g.get('db') is None or 'db' not in g._get_current_object().__dict__, \
            "close_db must remove 'db' from flask.g"
        conn2 = get_db()
        assert conn1 is not conn2, "After close_db, get_db() must return a new connection"

test_get_db_creates_new_connection_after_close_db()

tests.name: test_get_db_connection_not_shared_across_separate_request_contexts
preconditions: Flask app created with TESTING=True and a temp DATABASE path
Database initialised via init_db()
actions: Open first app context, call get_db(), store conn1, pop context
Open second app context, call get_db(), store conn2, pop context
Assert conn1 is not conn2 (different request contexts must not share connections)
expected: Each app context (simulating a separate request) produces a distinct connection object
Boundary: exactly one context boundary separates the two calls
trace: R-FLASKR-025: 'per request' scope — connection must not leak across request boundaries
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db, init_db

def test_get_db_connection_not_shared_across_separate_request_contexts():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite')
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        init_db()
    ctx1 = app.app_context()
    ctx1.push()
    conn1 = get_db()
    ctx1.pop()
    ctx2 = app.app_context()
    ctx2.push()
    conn2 = get_db()
    ctx2.pop()
    assert conn1 is not conn2, "Connections from separate request contexts must be distinct objects"

test_get_db_connection_not_shared_across_separate_request_contexts()

tests.name: test_get_db_g_db_key_absent_before_first_call
preconditions: Flask app created with TESTING=True and a temp DATABASE path
Database initialised via init_db()
A fresh app context is pushed but get_db() has NOT yet been called
actions: Push a fresh app context
Verify 'db' is not yet in g (boundary: zero calls)
Call get_db() exactly once (boundary: first call)
Verify 'db' is now in g and is the returned connection
expected: Before any call: g has no 'db' attribute
After exactly one call: g.db is the returned connection object
trace: R-FLASKR-025: 'if db not in g' guard — boundary at zero vs one call
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db, init_db
from flask import g

def test_get_db_g_db_key_absent_before_first_call():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite')
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        init_db()
    with app.app_context():
        # Before any get_db() call, 'db' must not be in g
        try:
            pre_val = g.db
            assert False, "g.db should not exist before get_db() is called"
        except AttributeError:
            pass  # expected: 'db' not yet in g
        conn = get_db()
        # After exactly one call, g.db must be the connection
        assert g.db is conn, "g.db must be set to the connection returned by get_db()"

test_get_db_g_db_key_absent_before_first_call()

Test client available

Assert HTTP 200 response (confirms the request lifecycle completed without db errors)

import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

def test_get_db_reuse_verified_via_http_request():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite')
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r1 = client.get('/')
    assert r1.status_code == 200, f"Expected 200, got {r1.status_code}"
    r2 = client.get('/')
    assert r2.status_code == 200, f"Expected 200 on second request, got {r2.status_code}"

tests.name: test_close_db_called_on_teardown_does_not_raise
preconditions: Flask app created with TESTING=True and a temp DATABASE path
Database initialised via init_db()
An active app context is pushed
actions: Push an app context WITHOUT calling get_db() (g has no 'db')
Call close_db() directly
Assert no exception is raised (g.pop('db', None) must handle missing key gracefully)
expected: close_db() with no prior get_db() call completes without raising any exception
Return value of close_db() is None (no side-effect)
trace: R-FLASKR-025: close_db uses g.pop with default None — must not raise on missing key
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db, close_db

def test_close_db_called_on_teardown_does_not_raise():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite')
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        init_db()
    with app.app_context():
        # Do NOT call get_db() — g has no 'db'
        try:
            result = close_db()
            assert result is None, "close_db() must return None"
        except Exception as exc:
            assert False, f"close_db() must not raise when 'db' absent from g, got: {exc}"

test_close_db_called_on_teardown_does_not_raise()
